title: Power-ups
summary: Add lives, a status bar, a gold turtle and an upgrade you buy with points.
language: python
modules: [ui]
hook: "Games and apps are built from the same parts: buttons that change state, and rules about what each change means."
app:
  command: "node \"$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs\" \"$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground\" 8123"
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8123/index.html"
  ready: Python code
  layout: full

explainClip:
  query: { code: "@powerups.py#solution", view: "output", autorun: 1, use: "ui" }
  caption: "Games are built from an interface and rules"
  say: "Games are built from two kinds of parts: an interface, and rules."
  pacing: { keyDelayMs: 22 }
  clip:
    - wait: 800
    - caption:
        text: "The interface: the status bar and the buttons you see."
        say: "The interface is what you see: the status bar and buttons."

        say: "One label function draws each part. Three calls, no copies."

Your game works. Now make it richer: lives instead of misses, a proper status bar, a gold turtle worth more, and an upgrade that costs points. Each one is a small change to the program you already have.

## Predict

```step
stage: predict
code: powerups.py#lives
check:
  type: predict
  q: "You start a game and miss three turtles in a row. What happens?"
  options: ["Nothing: misses are not counted", "Lives goes 3, 2, 1, 0 and the game stops with the Start button back", "The game ends after the first miss", "Lives goes below 0 and the game carries on"]
  actual: "Each miss takes a life. At 0, playing becomes False, so hop stops and the Start button is drawn again."
```

This is your game with **lives** in place of misses. Read `hide()`: what changes when the turtle escapes?

## Run

```step
stage: run
code: powerups.py#lives
try: { starter: "powerups.py#lives", height: 480 }
check: { type: reflect, text: "I played until I ran out of lives, and I can point to the line that ends the game." }
```

Press Start and miss on purpose. Then play properly and see how long you last.

## Investigate

```step
stage: investigate
code: powerups.py#lives
insight: "The same program has two kinds of parts: the user interface (show the state, let the player act) and the rules (what each event means). Naming them is the first step to both app and game design."
check:
  type: match
  q: "Each part of a game is user interface, a game rule, or both. Match them."
  pairs:
    - ["The status bar showing score, lives and time", "user interface: shows the state"]
    - ["The Start button", "user interface: the player acts"]
    - ["Losing a life when a turtle escapes", "game rule: what an event means"]
    - ["A gold turtle worth 5 points", "game rule: a reward"]
    - ["A button that costs 5 points to use", "both: a control that follows a rule"]
  explain: "Apps are mostly user interface around some rules; games are mostly rules with some user interface. You are building both."
```

Look at the program again: which lines draw things the player sees, and which lines decide what happens?

## Add the power-ups

```step
stage: modify
try: { starter: "powerups.py#status", height: 500 }
tasks:
  - starter: "powerups.py#status"
    hint:
      - "def label(x, y, name, value): goto(x, y), write(name), goto(x + 55, y), write(value)."
      - "In draw_scene: label(-190, 160, \"Score\", score), then Lives at -50 and Time at 90."
    check:
      type: code
      text: "A status bar drawn by one function with four parameters, used three times."
      rules: { contains: ["def label(x, y, name, value)", "\"Score\", score)", "\"Lives\", lives)", "\"Time\", time_left)"] }
  - starter: "powerups.py#gold"
    hint:
      - "In hop, after place changes: if place % 3 == 0: gold = True, else: gold = False."
      - "In draw_scene: if showing and gold: goto(tx, ty) then dot(50, \"gold\"). In clicked: if gold: score = score + 5, else: score = score + 1."
    check:
      type: code
      text: "Every third spot is gold, shown with a gold circle, and worth 5."
      rules: { contains: ["place % 3 == 0", "dot(50, \"gold\")", "score = score + 5"] }
  - starter: "powerups.py#upgrade"
    hint:
      - "Add delay = 1000 with the other variables, set it back to 1000 in start(), and use ontimer(hop, delay) and ontimer(hide, delay - 300)."
      - "In clicked: if playing and score >= 5 and inside(x, y, -60, -180, 120, 40): take 5 points, add 200 to delay, draw_scene()."
    check:
      type: code
      text: "A Slow (5) button that spends points to slow the turtle."
      rules: { contains: ["ontimer(hop, delay)", "score >= 5", "delay = delay + 200"] }
```

### Status bar

Write `label(x, y, name, value)` and use it to show **Score**, **Lives** and **Time** across the top. One function, three calls.

### Gold turtle

Every third spot, the turtle is gold: draw a gold circle under it, and make catching it worth **5**.

### Upgrade button

While playing, the button says **Slow (5)**. Clicking it spends 5 points and slows the turtle down by 200 milliseconds, but only if you can afford it.

## Make: your own power-up

```step
stage: make
try: { starter: "powerups.py#solution", height: 520 }
hint:
  - "More time: a button that costs 10 points and adds 5 to time_left."
  - "Bigger catch box: a power-up that makes the box 60 by 60 instead of 40 by 40 (remember to centre it: tx - 30)."
  - "Double points: a variable that doubles every catch until the next game."
check: { type: reflect, text: "I invented a power-up, gave it a cost, and can explain why the cost is fair." }
```

Invent a power-up of your own. Decide what it does, what it costs and when it can be used, then build it. Write one sentence (as a comment at the top) that explains why the cost is fair.

```teacher
summary: The second half of the final challenge. Students add lives, a status
  bar, a gold turtle worth 5 and an upgrade bought with points, then invent a
  power-up of their own.
time: 60
timing: Predict, Run and Investigate 15 min · Status bar 10 min · Gold turtle 10
  min · Upgrade 10 min · Your own power-up 15 min
goals:
  - I can tell which parts of a program are the user interface and which are the
    rules.
  - I can write a function with four parameters and use it several times.
  - I can add a rule that costs something, and explain why the cost is fair.
before: >
  This lesson mixes both directions students could take next. The **user
  interface** is what the player sees and uses (the status bar, the buttons);
  the **rules** decide what each event means (losing a life, gold is worth 5, an
  upgrade costs 5). The Investigate task sorts parts into the two kinds. Try the
  upgrade task yourself: it uses a variable `delay` instead of the fixed 1000
  milliseconds.
running:
  - "Predict: each miss takes a life; at 0 lives the game stops. Point to the
    line that ends the game."
  - "Investigate: discuss the match before checking it. 'Both' (a button that
    costs points) is the interesting one."
  - "Status bar: one function, label(x, y, name, value), called three times. Ask
    what the alternative would be (copying six lines three times)."
  - "Gold turtle: every third spot is gold, using % from Every other. The gold
    circle is drawn under the turtle."
  - "Upgrade: the button only works if score >= 5. Ask what happens without that
    check (scores go negative)."
  - "Your own power-up: students write one sentence at the top explaining why
    its cost is fair. Share a few."
stuck:
  - see: The upgrade can be bought with 0 points and the score goes negative.
    ask: What should be true before the player can buy it?
    fix: Add score >= 5 to the if that checks the button.
  - see: The gold circle stays on screen after the turtle moves on.
    ask: When is the gold circle drawn, and what clears it?
    fix: Draw it only when showing and gold are both True, and redraw (draw_scene)
      after a catch or a hide.
  - see: The upgrade button seems to do nothing.
    ask: Does hop() use delay, or still the number 1000?
    fix: Use ontimer(hop, delay) and ontimer(hide, delay - 300).
stretch: Add a power-up that makes the catch box bigger for 10 seconds, then
  switches back by itself (a timer).
support: Do the status bar together, then let students choose either the gold
  turtle or the upgrade rather than both.
leads: "Completing this and Catch the turtle marks the course Challenge
  complete. Optional next: Control panel (user interface, towards Gradio and web
  pages) or Game levels (games, towards MakeCode Arcade and microStudio)."
exit:
  q: Name one part of your game that is user interface and one that is a game
    rule.
  a: "For example: the status bar is user interface (it shows the state); losing a
    life on a miss is a game rule."
explain: >
  Games and apps are built from the same two kinds of parts. The **user
  interface** is what you see and use: the status bar, the buttons. The
  **rules** decide what each event means: a miss loses a life, a gold turtle is
  worth 5, an upgrade costs 5 points.


  `label(x, y, name, value)` is one function that draws one part of the status
  bar. Calling it three times draws Score, Lives and Time, with no copied code.


  A good power-up has a fair cost: strong enough to want, expensive enough to
  think about.
solutions:
  step-4#t1: powerups.py#sol-status
  step-4#t2: powerups.py#sol-gold
  step-4#t3: powerups.py#solution
  step-5: powerups.py#sol-own
struggle: Separating the rules from the display, and the check before buying.
  Ask what must be true before the player can buy, before they write the if.
```

# region: lives
from turtle import *
from ui import inside, draw_button

speed(0)
penup()
hideturtle()

xs = [-120, 0, 120, 120, 0, -120]
ys = [60, 110, 60, -50, -100, -50]
place = 0
tx = 0
ty = 0
score = 0
lives = 3
showing = False
time_left = 30
playing = False


def draw_scene():
    clear()
    goto(-190, 160)
    write(score, False, "left", ("Arial", 20, "normal"))
    goto(-20, 160)
    write(lives, False, "left", ("Arial", 20, "normal"))
    goto(150, 160)
    write(time_left, False, "left", ("Arial", 20, "normal"))
    if playing == False:
        draw_button(-60, -180, 120, 40, "Start")
    goto(tx, ty)


def hop():
    global place, tx, ty, showing
    if playing:
        tx = xs[place]
        ty = ys[place]
        place = (place + 1) % len(xs)
        goto(tx, ty)
        showturtle()
        showing = True
        ontimer(hide, 700)
        ontimer(hop, 1000)


def hide():
    global showing, lives, playing
    if showing:
        lives = lives - 1
        showing = False
        hideturtle()
        if lives == 0:
            playing = False
        draw_scene()


def tick():
    global time_left, playing
    if playing:
        time_left = time_left - 1
        if time_left == 0:
            playing = False
            hideturtle()
        else:
            ontimer(tick, 1000)
        draw_scene()


def start():
    global score, lives, time_left, playing, place
    score = 0
    lives = 3
    time_left = 30
    place = 0
    playing = True
    draw_scene()
    hop()
    ontimer(tick, 1000)


def clicked(x, y):
    global score, showing
    if playing and showing and inside(x, y, tx - 20, ty - 20, 40, 40):
        score = score + 1
        showing = False
        hideturtle()
        draw_scene()
    if playing == False and inside(x, y, -60, -180, 120, 40):
        start()


draw_scene()
onscreenclick(clicked)
listen()
mainloop()
# endregion

from turtle import *
from ui import inside, draw_button

speed(0)
penup()
hideturtle()

xs = [-120, 0, 120, 120, 0, -120]
ys = [60, 110, 60, -50, -100, -50]
place = 0
tx = 0
ty = 0
score = 0
lives = 3
showing = False
gold = False
time_left = 30
playing = False
delay = 1000


def label(x, y, name, value):
    goto(x, y)
    write(name, False, "left", ("Arial", 14, "normal"))
    goto(x + 55, y)
    write(value, False, "left", ("Arial", 14, "bold"))


def draw_scene():
    clear()
    label(-190, 160, "Score", score)
    label(-50, 160, "Lives", lives)
    label(90, 160, "Time", time_left)
    if playing:
        draw_button(-60, -180, 120, 40, "Slow (5)")
    else:
        draw_button(-60, -180, 120, 40, "Start")
    if showing and gold:
        goto(tx, ty)
        dot(50, "gold")
    goto(tx, ty)


def hop():
    global place, tx, ty, showing, gold
    if playing:
        tx = xs[place]
        ty = ys[place]
        place = (place + 1) % len(xs)
        if place % 3 == 0:
            gold = True
        else:
            gold = False
        showing = True
        draw_scene()
        showturtle()
        ontimer(hide, delay - 300)
        ontimer(hop, delay)


def hide():
    global showing, lives, playing
    if showing:
        lives = lives - 1
        showing = False
        hideturtle()
        if lives == 0:
            playing = False
        draw_scene()


def tick():
    global time_left, playing
    if playing:
        time_left = time_left - 1
        if time_left == 0:
            playing = False
            hideturtle()
        else:
            ontimer(tick, 1000)
        draw_scene()


def start():
    global score, lives, time_left, playing, place, delay
    score = 0
    lives = 3
    delay = 1000
    time_left = 30
    place = 0
    playing = True
    draw_scene()
    hop()
    ontimer(tick, 1000)


def clicked(x, y):
    global score, showing, delay
    if playing and showing and inside(x, y, tx - 20, ty - 20, 40, 40):
        if gold:
            score = score + 5
        else:
            score = score + 1
        showing = False
        hideturtle()
        draw_scene()
    if playing and score >= 5 and inside(x, y, -60, -180, 120, 40):
        score = score - 5
        delay = delay + 200
        draw_scene()
    if playing == False and inside(x, y, -60, -180, 120, 40):
        start()


draw_scene()
onscreenclick(clicked)
listen()
mainloop()
# endregion
